record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.context_brief: Wandering domains in a small-mass n-body regime
record.original_question: In the spatial n-body problem with one mass m₀ = 1 and the remaining masses m_j = εM_j for 1 ≤ j ≤ n−1, with all M_j > 0 and ε small, does every neighborhood of distinct coplanar circular orbits around m₀ moving in the same direction contain wandering domains?

evidence.quote: when ε is small, there are wandering domains .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian spatial n-body problem in $\mathbb{R}^3$, where $n\ge 3$ point masses $m_0,m_1,\dots,m_{n-1}$ interact via Newton's law of universal gravitation. Fix the masses by setting $m_0=1$ and $m_j=\varepsilon M_j$ for $1\le j\le n-1$, where $M_1,\dots,M_{n-1}$ are fixed positive constants and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter. Consider initial conditions in which the small bodies $m_1,\dots,m_{n-1}$ lie in a common plane through $m_0$ and each follows a Keplerian circular orbit around $m_0$, all with pairwise distinct radii and all revolving in the same direction (the unperturbed configuration of $n-1$ coplanar, codirectional circular orbits around the central mass).

A wandering domain for a flow $\phi^t$ on a phase space $X$ is a nonempty open set $U\subset X$ such that the sets $\phi^t(U)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, are pairwise disjoint for all sufficiently large $|t|$ (equivalently, $U$ is not contained in the nonwandering set of $\phi^t$).

Question: For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, does every neighborhood (in phase space) of such a configuration of distinct coplanar circular orbits around $m_0$ moving in the same direction contain a wandering domain of the n-body flow?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a definitive resolution of this specific question on the existence of wandering domains in neighborhoods of small-mass coplanar circular configurations in the spatial n-body problem. The problem appears to remain open; related results on Arnold diffusion and instability in the planetary problem exist but do not directly settle this formulation.

status_evidence.title: Four Open Questions for the N-Body Problem (Moeckel)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open questions about the Newtonian n-body problem including instability and diffusion phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: Instability/diffusion questions in the planetary n-body regime are listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Topics in Celestial Mechanics (Moeckel notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes covering the Newtonian n-body problem.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the existence of wandering domains near coplanar circular configurations is given.
